[SASRec](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1) already learns selective historical attention, favoring recent interactions on sparse datasets. Its controlled ablation supports retaining residual connections: removing them reduced Beauty NDCG@10 from 0.3142 to 0.2591. This supports preserving useful item information, but does not establish that gated recent-mean fusion beats convex interpolation. No directly matched controlled comparison emerged from the sources reviewed.

Mechanistically, additive fusion h + g·r retains coefficient 1 on the historical representation; it cannot explicitly attenuate that branch. Convex fusion (1−g)·h + g·r can reduce its coefficient as recency weight increases, although stale influence may remain inside h. These are architectural deductions, not measured gains. A proposed control is to normalize both branches consistently and monitor their norms, avoiding apparent gate preferences caused by scale differences. Initialize sigmoid gates with zero weights and a negative bias for a baseline-favoring start; zero bias gives g=0.5. An exactly zero-initialized residual scalar preserves the baseline initially, following [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887), whose evidence concerns optimization rather than recommendation accuracy.

The simplest informative ablation compares unchanged SASRec, fixed-weight convex recent-mean fusion, and learned convex fusion; then compare additive fusion using the same window, normalization, and initial recency weight. Pool only nonpadding items at or before each prediction position, dividing by valid counts. Combine causal and padding masks, explicitly handle fully masked padded queries, and zero padded outputs; [PyTorch MultiheadAttention](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.MultiheadAttention.html) uses True to block boolean-mask positions. Keep seeds, candidates, training budget, and checkpoint selection fixed; judge gains by the prescribed four-category macro validation HR@10.
